title: Execution Clearance Surface Design Decision
summary: Record the design decision not to implement a broad MCP-invocable global disable-switch clearing tool as the next step. Execution clearance is the highest-risk surface in the bridge and must not be treated like a normal convenience tool. The preferred first implementation direction is human-local operator-controlled clearance outside the model-callable MCP surface, with MCP tools limited to observing and validating that clearance rather than creating it.
caveats: This packet is a design decision only; no MCP bridge code is modified.
This packet does not create an execution-clearance tool.
This packet does not clear the disable switch.
This packet does not consume approval.
This packet does not contact the runner start endpoint, start OpenCode, or run FP-027.
The fresh FP-MCP-216 approval remains valid only until its expiry and must not be consumed while execution remains disabled.
A future implementation packet must separately design and verify the operator-local clearance mechanism before any execution attempt.
boundaries: MCP-invocable global disable-switch clearing approved: false
execution grant issued by this packet: false

riskRationale.coreConcern: A tool that clears the actual execution disable switch is the most consequential surface in the bridge. Treating it as a normal MCP-invocable action would put the final execution-enable act inside the same model-driven conversation channel that has already observed platform invocation blocks and surrounding field/packet scope ambiguities.
riskRationale.fp025Constraint: Execution enablement must remain packet-scoped, target-workspace-scoped, model-scoped, run-mode-scoped, time-boxed, human-approved, abortable, observable, and reversible. A broad boolean-like MCP tool would not satisfy that standard by construction.
riskRationale.fp194Constraint: New tool surfaces cannot be presumed safe merely because surrounding practice is careful. Execution-clearance tooling requires explicit structural reasoning before implementation, with stricter scrutiny than read-only diagnostic tools.

preferredFirstDesign.clearanceCreationSurface: human-local operator-controlled mechanism outside model-callable MCP tool surface
examples: manual local CLI command executed by operator on the machine
file-based signed or explicit local flag written by operator outside MCP
environment/local runner control state set by operator outside ChatGPT tool invocation
preferredFirstDesign.mcpRole: observe and validate clearance state only; do not create or relax it
requiredProperties: fails closed if stale or mismatched

minimumConstraints: the clearance tool itself must require a fresh approval tuple
must refuse missing/mismatched request id, approval id, model id, run mode, workspace, branch, and target commit
must write append-only clearance evidence rather than mutating existing approval/request artifacts
must include explicit expiration and automatic invalidation on repo commit drift
must not call runner start or consume approval in the same action
must be audited before use under FP-MCP-194-style structural equivalence rules

structuredRecord.nextImplementationDirection: Design operator-local clearance mechanism and MCP read-only validation of that mechanism; do not build a model-callable clearance mutator as the next step.
